unfold.unfolded: Let $V$ be an irreducible finite-dimensional representation of $G$, and let $\beta$ be the canonical basis of $V$. Let $J\subset I$, and let $V_J\subset V$ be the $L_J$-submodule spanned by the highest weight vector of $V$. Let $V_{\geqslant 0}=\sum_{b\in\beta}\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}\,b$ and $(V_J)_{\geqslant 0}=V_J\cap V_{\geqslant 0}$. Then for any $w\in W^J$ and $u\in U^-_{w,>0}$, we have $$u\cdot(V_J)_{\geqslant 0}=(u\cdot V_J)\cap V_{\geqslant 0}.$$
notes: The canonical basis, L_J, W^J, I and U^-_{w,>0} are not defined in the context, so they are kept as the paper writes them.
The phrase the L_J-submodule spanned by the highest weight vector is read as the smallest L_J-submodule containing that vector, as the paper writes it.
